title: Microcontrollers 101
description: Build real hardware projects with Arduino-compatible boards. Learn to read sensors, control LEDs, and debug electronic circuits from the ground up.

modules.title: Module 1: Electronics Foundations
modules.summary: Learn about voltage, current, resistance, and how microcontrollers work.

content.text: A microcontroller is a tiny computer on a single chip that can sense the world, make decisions, and control real hardware. This is the brain behind your washing machine, microwave, bike light, and thermostat.
Microcontroller vs Computer

A microcontroller is designed to do ONE job reliably, often for years without rebooting. Your laptop runs an operating system, manages windows, and waits for you to decide what happens next. A microcontroller usually runs one program forever.

content.title: You do not need to memorize electronics
content.text: Start with the working model: a pin can be an input or an output, and a program decides what to do with it. The details become familiar through building.

content.question: Which task best fits a microcontroller?
options: Watching a plant's soil moisture and sounding an alarm when it is dry
content.explanation: A microcontroller is ideal for a small, repeated, dedicated job such as monitoring a sensor and controlling an output.

content.text: Electricity is the flow of electrons through a conductor. Three key concepts you need to know: voltage, current, and resistance.

rows: Amount of water flowing per second

content.text: Ohm's Law connects these three: V = I × R. Voltage equals current times resistance. If you know any two values, you can calculate the third.

content.code:
V = I × R
Voltage = Current × Resistance

Example:
A 5V circuit with a 100Ω resistor:
I = 5V / 100Ω = 0.05A (50mA)

content.title: Never short a power pin to ground
content.text: Connecting 5V directly to GND without resistance can damage your board. Always have a component (LED, resistor, motor) between power and ground.

content.question: What does a 220Ω resistor do in a simple LED circuit?
options: Limits current so the LED and pin are not damaged
content.explanation: The resistor controls the current. It protects both the LED and the microcontroller pin.

content.text: A breadboard lets you prototype circuits without soldering. It has rows and columns that are internally connected.

items: Center column: Each hole in a 5-hole row is connected
Power rails: The long columns on the edges run the full length (usually red for +, blue for -)
Jumper wires: Connect components on the breadboard to your microcontroller pins

content.title: Build with power off
content.text: Always disconnect USB power before changing your circuit. This prevents accidental shorts that can damage components.

content.question: Which part of a breadboard connects all holes in a row together?
content.explanation: In a breadboard, each row of 5 holes is internally connected. Components plugged into the same row are electrically connected.

modules.title: Module 2: Your First Circuit
modules.summary: Build your first LED circuit and write your first Arduino program.

content.text: Your first circuit: an LED that blinks. You'll learn to wire an LED with a resistor and write your first Arduino sketch.

items.title: Disconnect power
items.text: Build with the USB cable unplugged.

items.title: Place the LED
items.text: Put the LED across the centre gap of the breadboard so its two legs are in different rows.

items.title: Add the resistor
items.text: Connect the resistor from the LED's anode row to a free row.

items.title: Wire the signal
items.text: Connect that free row to digital pin 8. Connect the LED's cathode row to GND.

items.title: Check, plug in, upload
items.text: Look for stray wires touching each other, then connect USB and upload the blink test.

content.title: LED polarity matters
content.text: The longer leg (anode) goes toward the resistor/power. The shorter leg (cathode) goes toward GND. If reversed, the LED won't light.

content.question: What does pinMode(LED_PIN, OUTPUT) do?
options: Sets the pin to send output signals
content.explanation: pinMode(LED_PIN, OUTPUT) configures the pin to send signals (output) rather than read them (input).

content.text: The Serial Monitor lets your board talk to your computer. It's the quickest way to see what your program is actually doing.

items.title: Connect USB
items.text: Plug your board into your computer.

items.title: Open Serial Monitor
items.text: In Arduino IDE: Tools > Serial Monitor, or click the magnifying glass icon.

items.title: Set baud rate
items.text: Make sure it says 9600 baud - this must match Serial.begin(9600) in your code.

items.title: Watch output
items.text: You should see counter values incrementing every second.

content.title: Baud rates must match
content.text: If you see garbage characters, the serial monitor baud rate doesn't match Serial.begin(). Change one to match the other.

content.question: What must match between Serial.begin() and the serial monitor?
content.explanation: Both sides must use the same communication speed, such as 9600 baud.

content.text: Combine three LEDs, timing, and structure to build a traffic light. This teaches state sequencing without needing a button yet.

content.title: Extension: Add a pedestrian button
content.text: When pressed, finish the current green phase safely, then switch to red after a short delay.

content.question: Why put the three output settings inside a showState() function?
options: Functions make the board run faster
It avoids repeating the same three lines and makes the states easier to read
Functions are required before using delay()
content.explanation: The function gives a name to a repeated action. The code becomes easier to read, test, and change.

modules.title: Module 3: Sensors and Analog Input
modules.summary: Learn to read analog sensors like light and temperature sensors.

content.text: Digital pins see HIGH or LOW. Analog inputs see a range. That range is what lets a microcontroller measure light, temperature, position, and sound.

content.title: Calibrate before you decide
content.text: Record your sensor's raw values in its real environment. A 'dark' reading in a bright room may never occur in a dark cupboard.

content.question: On a 5V, 10-bit analog input, what does a reading of 1023 represent?
content.explanation: The maximum raw value corresponds to the reference voltage, approximately 5V on this type of board.

content.text: A digital pin can only be fully on or fully off, yet an LED can appear dim. PWM switches the pin on and off very quickly.

content.title: analogWrite is not true analog
content.text: The pin still switches digitally. PWM only makes the average power adjustable.

content.question: What does analogWrite(pin, 127) do?
options: Switches the pin to an input
content.explanation: 127 is about half of the 0-255 range, so the pin is HIGH for roughly half of each PWM cycle.

content.text: Build a light that turns on when the room gets dark. Combines an analog sensor, threshold, and hysteresis.

content.title: Hysteresis prevents flicker
content.text: Without two thresholds (ON and OFF), a reading hovering around 650 could switch the light on and off rapidly.

content.question: Why use two thresholds instead of one?
options: To make the sensor more expensive
To prevent rapid on/off switching around a single threshold
Because analog pins require two values
content.explanation: Hysteresis adds a small dead band so small fluctuations don't cause the output to flicker.

modules.title: Module 4: Digital Input and Serial Communication
modules.summary: Buttons, pull-up resistors, serial debugging, and serial communication.

content.text: A button seems simple, but a floating input can behave unpredictably. A pull-up resistor gives the pin a known state when the button is not pressed.

content.title: Mechanical switches bounce
content.text: When a physical button closes, metal contacts can chatter for a few milliseconds. Debouncing means ignoring new changes for a short time.

content.question: With INPUT_PULLUP, what does an unpressed button read?
content.explanation: The pull-up holds the pin HIGH. Pressing connects it to GND, pulling it LOW.

content.text: Serial communication lets your board send text to your computer. Perfect for debugging and remote control.

content.question: Why wait for a newline before handling a serial command?
options: It ensures the whole command arrived
content.explanation: Characters arrive individually. Waiting for a line ending lets you process a complete command.

content.text: Build a plant monitor that reads soil moisture, shows status lights, and reports values over serial.

content.title: Extension ideas
content.text: Add a push button for manual reading, log to SD card, or add a Wi-Fi module for notifications.

content.question: Why calibrate a soil sensor in your own pot?
options: Because raw readings depend on sensor, soil, and power conditions
content.explanation: Sensor output varies between setups. Calibration turns a generic device into a measurement you can trust.

modules.title: Module 5: Troubleshooting and Best Practices
modules.summary: Debugging circuits, reading datasheets, and project documentation.

content.text: Debugging is narrowing the space between what you expected and what is actually happening.

rows: USB cable, port selection, driver, board type
Polarity, resistor placement, pin number, code
Power, shared ground, wrong analog pin, wiring

content.title: Change one thing at a time
content.text: After each change, test again. Several simultaneous changes make results impossible to interpret.

content.question: What is the best first step when a circuit does not work?
options: Change all the code at once
Describe the actual behaviour and isolate the failing layer
content.explanation: Careful observation narrows the problem. Test power, wiring, input, code, and output one layer at a time.

content.text: A datasheet is a reference manual. Learn to find absolute maximum ratings, operating conditions, pin descriptions, and application circuits.

rows: What range should I actually use?
What does a known-good circuit look like?

content.title: The board's 5V pin is not unlimited
content.text: The regulator and USB port have current limits. Motors, servos, and LED strips should usually have their own power supply.

content.question: Which datasheet section tells you if a sensor's signal pin is safe with a 5V board?
options: The absolute maximum ratings and logic-level specifications
content.explanation: These sections define the voltages the part can tolerate and the levels it considers high or low.

content.text: Review everything: microcontroller basics, circuits, serial communication, sensors, PWM, and debugging.

items: Can you explain what a microcontroller does?
Can you wire an LED with a resistor?
Can you read an analog sensor?
Can you use serial monitor to debug?
Can you build the plant monitor?

content.title: Final project: Plant Monitor
content.text: Build a plant monitor that reads soil moisture, shows status with LEDs, and reports values over serial. Add calibration and comments to your code.

content.question: Why calibrate a soil sensor in your own pot?
options: Because raw readings depend on sensor, soil, and power conditions
content.explanation: Sensor output varies between setups. Calibration turns a generic device into a measurement you can trust.

finalAssessment.title: Circuit Starter Assessment
finalAssessment.intro: Answer all 8 questions. You need 80% to pass and unlock the Circuit Starter badge and certificate. You can retake the assessment if needed.

questions.question: What is the main role of a microcontroller?
options: Run a full desktop operating system
questions.explanation: Microcontrollers are designed for focused, repeated tasks such as reading sensors and controlling outputs.

questions.question: What does a 220 ohm resistor do in a simple LED circuit?
questions.explanation: The resistor protects the LED and microcontroller pin by limiting current.

questions.question: Which section of setup() runs once at startup?
questions.explanation: setup() runs once; loop() runs repeatedly.

questions.question: With INPUT_PULLUP, what does an unpressed button usually read?
questions.explanation: The internal pull-up holds the input HIGH until the button pulls it to GND.

questions.question: Which Arduino function reads a changing analog voltage?
questions.explanation: analogRead() returns a number representing the voltage on an analog input.

questions.question: What is hysteresis used for in the night-light project?
questions.explanation: Hysteresis uses separate on and off thresholds to avoid rapid switching.

questions.question: Why should a motor often have its own power supply?
options: Motors can draw more current than the board can safely supply
questions.explanation: Motor current can exceed the board's regulator capacity and cause resets or damage.

questions.question: What is the best first step when a circuit does not work?
options: Change all the code at once
Describe the actual behaviour and isolate the failing layer
questions.explanation: Careful observation narrows the problem. Test power, wiring, input, code, and output one layer at a time.
